summary.intent: Plan and execute phase 63 (Read-Chain Navigation and Rotation Core) of the CipherBox project, then ship it via /ship-phase 63.
summary.outcome: Planning completed fully and verified (7 plans in 4 waves, all requirements and decisions covered). Execution reached mid-Wave 2 (3/7 plans done: 63-01, 63-02, 63-03), with Wave 2 plan 63-04 dispatched but not yet confirmed complete in the transcript.

repo: sdk-core has no `typecheck` script; the real type gate is `build` which runs `tsup && tsc -p tsconfig.build.json`. Plans 63-05/63-06 incorrectly reference a `typecheck` script.
Commit signing was already disabled (commit.gpgsign: false) at the repo level — no action needed for AFK sessions.
The GSD commit helper consistently reports a false-negative (exit code nonzero) but commits land correctly; verified via `git log`.
The project has documented worktree pitfalls (node_modules leaks, api:generate leaks) — sequential main-tree execution is preferred for tightly coupled plans.
CI health-poll for the local API server uses `curl -fsS http://localhost:3000/health` on port 3000 — mirrors the pattern for robust startup waits.
Phase 63 rotation engine landed in a named `engine.ts` (513 lines, 83% coverage, 18 tests) with 4 named Phase-64 seams for future extension.
PATTERNS.md was committed by the planner subagent (dfaa43227), not the orchestrator — planner takes ownership of that artifact.
Drift gate flagged a stale `.planning/codebase/` map but is non-blocking at plan time when CONTEXT.md + RESEARCH.md carry verified implementation-site references.

code.finding: Replaced fragile `sleep 12` API startup wait with a bounded health-poll loop mirroring CI's curl pattern against localhost:3000/health.
Open Questions section needed `(RESOLVED)` markers to clear the plan-checker blocker; questions were substantively answered but not formally marked.
VALIDATION.md per-task verification map must be filled with actual task IDs and automated commands before plan-checker passes; leaving it as template body triggers a WARNING.

workflow: GSD plan-checker runs in two iterations when fixes are deterministic (formatting/tracking blockers with no design judgment needed) — fix inline and re-spawn rather than escalating to the planner.
Pattern-mapper produces 10/10 analogs before the planner runs; this is a mandatory gate in the plan-phase workflow.
Nyquist VALIDATION.md is created at step 5.5 with frontmatter only; the per-task body is populated after planning, not before.
Sequential wave execution (no worktrees) is the safe default when plans share test files or have barrel dependencies.
Wave 1 tsc build gate after execution is a cheap integration check before committing to Wave 2 — worth running even when no typecheck script exists.

friction: GSD commit helper consistently reports false-negative exit codes, requiring `git log` verification after every commit — creates noise and slows down the orchestrator.
sdk-core `typecheck` script referenced in plans 63-05 and 63-06 does not exist; executor subagents will need to be redirected to `build` instead.
VALIDATION.md template body must be manually filled post-planning — easy to forget, triggers a plan-checker WARNING if left as template.
API-SURFACE regeneration returned 0 symbols for sdk-core — the tool may not support this package type, making the intel gate a no-op.
Drift gate fires on stale codebase map even when CONTEXT.md/RESEARCH.md are verified current — creates a false alarm that must be manually assessed as non-blocking.
open_items: Plans 63-05 and 63-06 reference a non-existent `typecheck` script in sdk-core — executor subagents for these plans need to use `build` instead.
Phase 63 execution was still in progress at Wave 2 (63-04 dispatched, 63-05/06/07 not yet run) — waves 2-4 and /ship-phase 63 remain incomplete.
4 named Phase-64 seams created in the rotation engine (engine.ts) — these are intentional extension points deferred to Phase 64.
Codebase map is stale (drift gate fires) — a full map refresh was deferred as non-blocking at plan time and should be done separately.
